I honestly have been contemplating Linux, but this really is not very helpful. Which distribution is comparable to Windows? Can I play all my games (Battle.net and Steam) on there? How do I get it?

There are a lot of distributions, but the only ones good for gaming are probably the Debian based ones. Games can and will run on other versions, but most games are optimized for Ubuntu (a variant of Debian) if they have a Linux version available at all.

For games without a Linux version, they might run with a program called Wine, but the amount of tweaking you have to do is ridiculous. It might take hours for you to get a game running at all. Also, GPU drivers for Linux are terrible. They are usable, but nowhere near the performance that they get on WIndows. Typically, Nvidia drivers are better than AMD drivers, and there are open-source and closed-source drivers for both. Closed source is usually better for performance tasks but sometimes open-source drivers may run better.

I don't know about now, but it used to be a real pain in the ass to get Battle.net to run on Linux at all, at least for me. Steam is fine since it has a Linux client but you're going to miss out on a ton of games, especially indie games (there is an indie Linux game scene but most indie developers are going to focus on Windows for market share).

The easiest version of Linux to use it Ubuntu, you can get it off their site. Hopefully you get lucky with drivers and Ubuntu's own driver finder will work for you, but in the case it doesn't, be prepared to spend hours working on it.

Also some issues that I've had with Ubuntu specifically: I've never gotten Wine to run on Ubuntu at all, and Steam sometimes dies also. If that doesn't work, you can use SteamOS, but the user interface for it is absolute garbage.

Also, most distributions of Linux require you to disable secure-boot, which I find really annoying. The three that don't (as far as I know) are Ubuntu, OpenSUSE, and Fedora.

If you want to try out Linux, go for it, but for gaming Windows is still the best.

All Valve games are ported to Linux so they'll run fine, except for Dota 2: Unborn because that has issues on Windows as well. Installing them and getting them to run at all should be no problem, though.
